_comment_: Production overrides for the AgentBoard Proposal Worker.
Drop this file beside AgentBoard.Node.exe in the publish
output directory (e.g. C:\AgentBoard\ProposalWorker\). .NET
automatically loads appsettings.{DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT}.json.
What this file does vs. appsettings.json:
* Fills in Node.Id (stable per-machine identifier; the value
ends up in /health worker_id so the server can route follow-up
work to the same worker).
* Registers the worker with the FastAPI server: AgentBoard.ServerUrl
+ AgentBoard.StartupToken are REQUIRED. With RequireRegistration=true
the worker FAILS FAST at startup when ServerUrl / RabbitMq.Uri is
missing or no WorkBuddy/Codex agent could be registered - instead of
silently skipping and leaving every Story stuck in todo.
* Agents.* use explicit Command + AgentId. Command is NOT left empty:
an empty Command makes WorkerStartupService skip that agent entirely,
so the scheduler never sees it even when the CLI is installed.
* Agents.*.AgentBoardToken gives each logical agent its own FastAPI
service-user token. Reviewer isolation (assign_task_reviewer excludes
candidates whose user_id equals the task assignee) REQUIRES distinct
identities per agent: register one FastAPI user per agent (e.g.
service-user-wb / service-user-codex), put both into the project as
members, and paste their tokens here. Empty = falls back to the
shared AgentBoard.StartupToken, which breaks multi-agent review on a
single worker.
* Hardens Portal.Urls (binds 0.0.0.0 only if you also need LAN
access; otherwise keep 127.0.0.1).
What this file does NOT do:
* It does not store API keys. Set MINIMAX_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY
in the node process environment (the installer persists a
per-service environment block). See scripts/install-node.ps1.
P7b (2026-09-03): "Node" is the canonical section - configure here.
Program.cs binds "Worker" first (legacy baseline, see appsettings.json)
and then layers "Node" on top, overriding only keys that are actually
present and non-empty, so installs that have not been migrated yet keep
their operator-configured "Worker" values. Do NOT duplicate values into
both sections - the "Node" copy wins. scripts/install-node.ps1 mirrors
"Node" into "Worker" at install time so a rollback to the previous
binary keeps the same configuration.
